La Bola Negra

35mm

Book Now Book Now
  • Overview
  • Book Tickets
  • Credits
  • Also Playing

A big, old-school historical melodrama channeling an unfinished Lorca play gets a thrillingly modern, queer makeover in this second feature from powerhouse writer-director duo Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (in their native Spain, they’re known as “Los Javis”). Juggling three timelines and three gay protagonists across 1937, 1932, and 2017, this supremely confident and richly crafted triptych is much more than the sum of its parts — though working out quite how they interlock is a key pleasure.

The film’s backbone is its war story: Sebastian (played by singer Guitarricadelafuente) is conscripted into the fascist forces and ordered to befriend a leftist prisoner (Miguel Bernardeau) who refuses to share information. Five years earlier, Carlos (Milo Quifes) is blackballed from his father’s club for his sexual proclivities. And in 2017, writer-historian Alberto (Carlos Gonzalez) receives a surprising bequest…

A bold and exhilarating work, this dark-horse Competition entry came away with the Directing prize at Cannes.

Los Javis execute this mighty vision with thrilling technical bravado. Nearly every shot in the film is a carefully composed wonder […] It’s a dazzlingly assured film, delivering the heady satisfaction of seeing something ambitious actually land its nervy attempt.

Richard Lawson, Hollywood Reporter

Director

Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo

Cast

Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Lola Dueñas, Penélope Cruz, Glenn Close

House of Hope

Dir. Marjolein Busstra
93 min

"House of Hope" is the name of a Waldorf elementary school near Jerusalem in the occupied West Bank, founded by Manar and her husband Milad. This documentary follows their efforts to go about their lives before, during, and after the events of October 7.

Mon Oct 19, Tue Oct 20, Fri Oct 23, Sat Oct 24
VIFF Centre - Lochmaddy Studio Theatre

NAZA

NAZA

Dir. Yuval Abraham, Rachel Szor
80 min
Festival Encores

NAZA is a codeword euphemistically used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians it expects will be killed in an airstrike. This chilling documentary exposes the policy and process of state-sanctioned mass killings.

Mon Oct 19, Tue Oct 20, Wed Oct 21, Thu Oct 22, Sat Oct 24

VIFF thanks the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam), Sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Squamish), and səlilwətaɬ/Selilwitulh (Tsleil-Waututh) Nations for their continued stewardship of the unceded and occupied land on which our work takes place. As an organization founded and predominantly directed by settlers and immigrants, we understand our responsibility to seek out and build authentic relationships with Indigenous communities, and to allow this ongoing dialogue to influence our practices. As part of this process, we remain committed to collaborating with and supporting Indigenous artists, filmmakers, curators, and audiences.
